title: Green Mountains, Now Black
program_note:
The name Monteverdi means, of course, green mountain.  I was working on this treatment of excerpts from Monteverdi’s Orfeo and L’incoronazione di Poppea just as the Los Angeles fires were burning, though, so it seemed particularly thoughtless to be working on such a composition, until I realized that the mournfulness found in so much of Monteverdi’s music could be directed toward the situation at hand.  This is especially true of “Non Morir” (“Don’t Die!”) and “A Dio, Roma” (“Goodbye, Rome”) from Poppea, but could also be said of “Possente Spirto” (“Mighty Spirit”) from Orfeo, in which Orpheus in the netherworld begs to bring his dead wife back to the world of the living.
The one excerpt that does not fit this mold is “Pur Ti Miro” (“I Gaze Upon You”), the love duet at the end of Poppea, but then, it scarcely fits into the original opera at all — not least because it was probably not composed by Monteverdi, but also because the aria celebrates the culmination of Poppea’s and Nero’s scheming to divorce and depose Octavia, Nero’s wife, and install Poppea in her stead, which would prove to be only a brief moment of joy in her life (as she would live scarcely three more years).  In Green Mountains, Now Black the displacement of Octavia by Poppea is rectified by the music:  “A Dio Roma” is played simultaneously with and then winds up displacing “Pur Ti Miro,” It thus ends the quartet on a sad note, as we bid farewell to our beloved city.
Green Mountains, Now Black was commissioned by Coretet for Yarlung Artists, and was written for Quartet Integra.
The duration of the quartet is about 13 minutes:  6’40”, 2’10”, and 4’10.

David S. Lefkowitz
8 February, 2025
Los Angeles, CA
